change_of_basis: The earlier TS11 report said no third-party scanner existed on this host and produced SELF-AUTHORED results. That was true of the five named tools, but two of them are pip-installable, so they were installed and run: detect-secrets and pip-licenses. The self-authored results are now a fallback, not the primary evidence.

detect-secrets.scope: the six SP ZIPs and their unpacked members
detect-secrets.noise_disclosure: a first run over the whole build output reported 37 'Hex High Entropy String' hits, ALL of them inside the SBOM/licence JSON this round generated - i.e. its own sha256 values. Scanning a scanner's own report is noise; the scoped run over the deliverable found 0.

pip-licenses.scope: installed distributions in the working interpreter

still_absent.syft: no SBOM generator (the CycloneDX-shaped file is self-authored)
still_absent.consequence: no dependency-vulnerability claim of any kind can be made for this round

claim_ceiling: Two of five supply-chain checks are now third-party and both pass on the deliverable; SBOM and vulnerability scanning remain unavailable, so the release is still not qualified.
